mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for two consecutive months signals a restrictive monetary policy stance, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the negative rank IC falls below 0.05.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincident with a housing starts (HOUST) contraction of more than 10% month-over-month signals weakening aggregate demand, which depresses corporate revenues and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the mechanism fails to activate more than once every five years.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 3.5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but no negative return occurs in any instance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates weakening manufacturing activity, which reduces corporate earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate within a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp monthly decline in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below 1% while the federal funds rate remains above 3% for two months signals disinflation under restrictive policy, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL MoM < 1% AND FEDFUNDS > 3% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but no negative return occurs in any activation.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in real personal savings (RSAFS) above 5% while personal income growth (proxied by GDPC1 growth) is below 1% signals a shift from spending to saving, which reduces aggregate demand and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the trigger activates but no negative return follows in any instance.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly payroll employment growth (PAYEMS) increase below 50,000 persons for three consecutive months signals a stalling labor market, which reduces wage growth and corporate cost pressures, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of triggered episodes, or the trigger does not activate within a 5-year period.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in housing starts (HOUST) above 10% while unemployment rate (UNRATE) is below 4% signals a constructive demand shock in the housing sector during a tight labor market, which boosts construction-related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
regime_hint: tight labor market with housing recovery
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 70% of triggered episodes, or the trigger fires but no positive return occurs in any activation.
